summary:
I surveyed 30+ JS charting libraries. Versions, licences and dates come from the live npm registry on 2026-10-14; gzip sizes were measured on the real dist files. Every candidate's classic-script build was smoke-tested from file:// in headless Chromium 141.

**Primary engine: Apache ECharts 6.1.0** (Apache-2.0, ASF-governed, 67.5k stars). Use the full UMD dist/echarts.min.js (359 KB gz), which is already vendored. That choice is confirmed.
- It is the only permissive engine that covers nearly the whole IB chart vocabulary in one classic script. That includes calendar, parallel, geo, sankey, treemap, sunburst, boxplot, candlestick and gauge.
- ECharts 6 added chord, beeswarm/jitter, axis breaks, a matrix coordinate system, runtime setTheme() and reusable custom series. All were verified working under file://.
- It has both an SVG renderer and a canvas renderer. The SVG renderer printed to PDF as vector with selectable text. Canvas printed as a ~104 ppi raster, but handled 200k points with LTTB in about 290 ms.
- Node SSR (renderToSVGString) runs from the same UMD file.

**Pitchbook recipes in ECharts:** a 6-chart pitchbook page all rendered cleanly:
- EBITDA bridge with connectors and a v6 axis break
- Marimekko and football field
- 4-dimension bubble via visualMap
- CAGR bracket

Waterfall, Mekko and football field are custom-series recipes of 20–40 lines, not native series.

**Complements:**
- @echarts-x/custom-* series (violin, bar-range, line-range, contour), adopt as needed.
- uPlot 1.6.32 (21 KB gz) for table sparklines and >1M-point series.
- D3 7.9 as a utility layer (d3-format, scale, hierarchy, geo).
- A lazy-loaded Vega-Lite 6.5 / Vega 6.4 / vega-embed 7.3 stack (~275 KB gz) for an optional explore/ask console. It has the best declarative cross-filtering, is the most LLM-friendly grammar, and interoperates with Altair. Keep it out of printed pages.
- echarts-gl only if 3D vol surfaces are needed.
- Plotly.js 4.1.2 only for plotly.py parity or scientific charts. It is heavy: 1.44 MB gz full, 422 KB finance bundle.

**Avoid:**
- ApexCharts went proprietary in 5.1.0 and is free only under US$2M revenue; the last MIT release is 5.0.0.
- AG Charts Community lacks waterfall, sankey, heatmap, box, candlestick, radar, funnel, treemap, zoom, navigator and animation; I confirmed these trigger Enterprise warnings.
- Highcharts, amCharts 5 (logo linkware) and ZingChart (watermark) are commercial; use them as reference only.
- Lightweight Charts carries a mandatory TradingView attribution notice and link.
- React-only libraries (Recharts, Nivo, visx) are out, since React 19 dropped UMD builds.
- Stale or broken: Taucharts, Frappe, C3, Britecharts, Toast UI, Vizzu (ESM+WASM fails on file://) and Unovis (no UMD).

AntV G2 5.4 and VisActor VChart 2.1 are strong MIT alternatives with native Mekko/mosaic, waterfall and storytelling motion. They are canvas-first, Chinese-first in docs, corporate-governed and heavier (VChart 617 KB gz). Borrow ideas from them; don't switch.

libraries.name: Apache ECharts
libraries.capabilities:
Native coverage of nearly every IB chart type in one script:
- bar, line, scatter, pie, sankey
- chord (new in v6), treemap with drill-down, sunburst
- boxplot, candlestick, heatmap, calendar, parallel
- radar, funnel, gauge, graph (force/circular)
- geo/map choropleth with scatter, lines and flows
- themeRiver, pictorialBar, tree

Also new in v6: matrix coordinate layout, beeswarm/jitter and axis breaks.

Waterfall, Marimekko and football field are custom-series recipes (verified). SVG and canvas renderers. Node SSR via renderToSVGString.
libraries.interactions_animation:
Interaction:
- dataZoom (inside and slider)
- brush (rect, polygon, lineX/Y) with events
- echarts.connect for linked tooltips and zoom
- legend filtering
- setOption diff updates, with replaceMerge for data swaps
- universalTransition morphs and label valueAnimation
- runtime setTheme (v6)
- large-data sampling (LTTB) and progressive rendering

Animation is among the best of the OSS engines.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding:
visualMap maps any data dimension to colour, colorAlpha, lightness, saturation, symbolSize, symbol or opacity.
- Several visualMaps can target different dimensions (6.1 seriesTargets).
- symbolSize and itemStyle callbacks give per-point encodings.
- decal patterns act as an extra categorical channel.
- A geo instance combines proportional symbols, choropleth and flow lines.
libraries.offline_classic_script:
Yes. Verified on file:// in Chromium 141.
- dist/echarts.min.js is the full UMD build; echarts.common.min.js and echarts.simple.min.js are lighter UMD builds.
- theme/*.js and i18n/lang*.js are UMD.
- Maps must be registered from a JS global; fetching them fails on file://.
libraries.size: 1095 KB min / 359 KB gz (full); 233 KB gz common; 164 KB gz simple
libraries.reason:
It is the only permissive, ASF-governed engine with near-complete IB coverage in one classic script.
- Dual SVG/canvas rendering gives vector print and big-data performance; both were verified.
- It has the deepest theming of the OSS engines, plus runtime setTheme.
- Interaction is mature.
- Node SSR fallback works.
- pyecharts 2.1 targets v6.

The gaps (waterfall, Mekko, football field, CAGR annotations) are proven 20–40-line custom series.

libraries.name: ECharts custom series (@echarts-x/custom-*)
libraries.capabilities: Official reusable custom series for ECharts 6: violin, contour, stage (sleep-stage/gantt-like), segmentedDoughnut, barRange, lineRange, liquidFill and wordCloud.
libraries.interactions_animation: Inherits ECharts tooltip and animation.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Same as ECharts (via api.visual and encode).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/<name>.auto.min.js is UMD and auto-registers on the global echarts.
libraries.reason: Tiny, official add-ons that fill the remaining gaps: violin, ranges/gantt, contour and segmented doughnut. They also show the registerCustomSeries pattern our kit should use for waterfall, Mekko and range series.

libraries.name: ECharts GL
libraries.capabilities: WebGL 3D for ECharts: surface (e.g. vol surfaces), bar3D, scatter3D, globe and 3D geo.
libraries.interactions_animation: 3D orbit rotate and zoom.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x/y/z position plus visualMap colour and size.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/echarts-gl.min.js is UMD and needs echarts loaded first.
libraries.reason: Optional. Use only if 3D vol surfaces or a globe are ever needed. WebGL output prints as a raster.

libraries.name: D3
libraries.capabilities: Low-level toolkit: scales, formats, shapes, hierarchy, geo projections, force layout, zoom/brush behaviours. Any bespoke chart can be built on it.
libraries.interactions_animation: d3-zoom, d3-brush and d3-transition primitives; all wiring is DIY.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/d3.min.js is UMD (global d3).
libraries.reason: Too low-level to be the kit engine for 50+ components. Valuable as an optional utility layer (d3-format for financial formats, scale/chromatic, hierarchy, d3-sankey maths, geo) and for bespoke one-off SVG exhibits.

libraries.name: uPlot
libraries.capabilities: Very fast canvas time-series and xy line, area, bars and points; handles about 1M points.
libraries.interactions_animation: Drag-zoom, cursor sync across charts and series toggle. No animation.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Minimal: per-series stroke and fill; points via plugins.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/uPlot.iife.min.js plus uPlot.min.css. Verified (requires a valid Intl locale).
libraries.reason: Lightweight complement for dozens of sparklines in comps or league tables, and for tick histories over 1M points, where an ECharts instance per cell is too heavy. Canvas only, so print needs a high-DPR snapshot.

libraries.name: Vega-Lite + Vega + vega-embed
libraries.capabilities:
Declarative grammar-of-graphics.
- Marks: bar, line, area, point, rect/heatmap, boxplot, arc, geoshape, text, rule, tick.
- Layer, facet, concat and repeat composition.
- Rich transforms: window, calculate expressions, fold, pivot, density, loess, regression.
- Vega adds treemap, partition and force layouts.
- No sankey, chord, radar or gauge.
libraries.interactions_animation: params selections (interval/point), bind:'scales' zoom and pan, legend binding and cross-view filtering. This is the best declarative cross-filter of any library. No real animation (only an experimental time encoding).
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, color, size, shape, opacity, strokeDash, row/column facet; fully declarative.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. build/vega.min.js, build/vega-lite.min.js and build/vega-embed.min.js are still UMD, even though Vega 6 is 'ESM-only' at package level. Verified on file://.
libraries.reason:
Use as a lazy-loaded complement for an explore/ask console.
- Native cross-filtering.
- The most LLM-friendly, schema-validatable chart grammar.
- Altair interop for Python analysts.

Not suitable as the pitchbook engine: no animation, missing IB types, alphabetical default sort and an academic look.

libraries.name: Plotly.js
libraries.capabilities:
Broad scientific and financial coverage:
- waterfall, funnel, candlestick/OHLC, indicator gauges
- sankey, treemap, sunburst, icicle
- parcoords and parcats, splom, contour, violin
- 3D surface, geo choropleth, quiver (new in v4)

No chord, calendar or force graph. Partial bundles are available (finance 436 KB gz).
libraries.interactions_animation: Excellent built-in interaction: drag-zoom, pan, rangeslider, box/lasso select events, hover modes and a modebar with SVG/PNG export. Animation is limited (Plotly.animate).
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: marker.size, color, symbol and opacity arrays; colorscales; facets via subplots.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. plotly.min.js and the partial *-dist-min bundles are UMD (global Plotly). Geo traces fetch topojson from cdn.plot.ly unless preloaded via window.PlotlyGeoAssets.
libraries.size: 1441 KB gz full; 422 KB gz finance; 388 KB gz basic
libraries.reason:
Optional, narrow complement for plotly.py parity or scientific charts (parcats, splom, 3D).
- Very heavy.
- Limited motion.
- The default look needs heavy templating to match a pitchbook.
- v4 brought breaking colour-parser changes (culori) and removed the mapbox traces.

libraries.name: AntV G2
libraries.capabilities:
Grammar-of-graphics with a rich mark library, verified via stdlib introspection:
- interval, cell, boxplot, sankey, chord, treemap
- partition (sunburst), pack, tree, forceGraph
- gauge, liquid, wordCloud, beeswarm, geo

flexX transform gives Marimekko. Broken Y axis since 5.4.0.
libraries.interactions_animation: Interactions: brushFilter, sliderFilter, sliderWheel, scrollbar, legendFilter and drillDown. elementPointMove lets users drag a point to edit data. Animations include morphing, growIn and waveIn.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Declarative encode for x, y, color, size, shape and opacity, plus facets.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/g2.min.js (canvas) was verified on file://. SVG needs g2.lite.min.js with @antv/g and @antv/g-svg UMD; full and lite cannot co-exist.
libraries.reason:
Strong, MIT, native Mekko, chord and sankey. Kept as reference rather than primary:
- canvas-first, which is worse for print
- Chinese-first docs
- Ant Group governance
- no calendar or native candlestick

Borrow its flexX, drag-to-edit and morphing ideas.

libraries.name: VisActor VChart
libraries.capabilities:
Spec-driven charts, including:
- native waterfall and mosaic (Marimekko)
- sankey, treemap, sunburst, circlePacking, boxPlot, heatmap
- funnel, gauge, radar, rose, venn, wordCloud, liquid, map
- rangeColumn, progress, correlation

Candlestick is in vchart-extension.
libraries.interactions_animation: dataZoom, brush, scrollBar and a storytelling player. Very rich animation. updateSpec does in-place updates.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Spec fields for x, y, series, size and colour, with visual-channel mappings.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. build/index.min.js is UMD (global VChart; use VChart.default). Verified on file://.
libraries.reason:
Best motion and storytelling of the MIT libraries, and it has native waterfall and mosaic. But:
- it is the heaviest bundle
- canvas only (SVG via a separate plugin)
- Chinese-first docs
- ByteDance origin may trigger vendor-risk review

Use as a design reference; VMind is a Step-2 LLM reference.

libraries.name: Observable Plot
libraries.capabilities:
Concise SVG grammar.
- Marks: bar, rect, cell, dot, line, area, geo, hexbin, density, contour, waffle, box, tree, link, difference.
- dodge transform gives beeswarm.
- Faceting with fx/fy.
libraries.interactions_animation: Pointer, tip and crosshair only. No zoom, no brush-filter, no animation.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: x, y, fill, stroke, r, opacity, symbol and fx/fy facets.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/plot.umd.min.js plus d3.min.js. Verified on file://.
libraries.size: 204 KB min / 67 KB gz (+90 KB gz d3)
libraries.reason: Beautiful static exploratory graphics with a slow 0.x release cadence (none since Feb 2025). It lacks zoom, cross-filter and motion, and ordinal axes sort alphabetically by default. ECharts covers its use cases.

libraries.name: Chart.js
libraries.capabilities:
Core types: bar, line, area, scatter, bubble, pie/doughnut, radar, polarArea.

Plugins verified on file://: sankey, treemap, matrix/heatmap, boxplot/violin, zoom, datalabels, annotation. Also available: geo, financial (stale) and parallel-coordinates plugins.
libraries.interactions_animation: Good default animations; zoom via plugin; no brush or cross-filter.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Bubble radius and per-point colours, set manually.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/chart.umd.min.js plus plugin UMDs. Verified.
libraries.reason: Canvas only, so print is raster. Breadth relies on unevenly maintained plugins (datalabels last released 2022; financial 0.2.1 from 2024). No calendar, chord, parallel or axis breaks. Fine for tiny embeds, wrong as the pitchbook engine.

libraries.name: billboard.js
libraries.capabilities: D3-based C3 successor: line, spline, step, area-range, bar, bubble, candlestick, donut, pie, gauge, funnel, polar, radar, scatter, treemap. 4.0 added an opt-in canvas mode for dense charts.
libraries.interactions_animation: Zoom, subchart navigator, regions and D3 transitions; PNG export.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Bubble size and per-series colour; limited.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/billboard.pkgd.min.js bundles d3 and was verified.
libraries.size: 810 KB min / 267 KB gz (pkgd); 153 KB gz without d3
libraries.reason: SVG output with CSS-class theming is attractive, but the chart vocabulary is too narrow (no sankey, sunburst, heatmap, geo, parallel or chord) to justify alongside ECharts.

libraries.name: AG Charts Community
libraries.capabilities:
Community edition: bar, line, area, scatter, bubble, histogram, pie and donut only.

Enterprise only (verified in-browser warnings): waterfall, sankey, heatmap, box-plot, candlestick, radar, funnel, treemap, chord and maps.
libraries.interactions_animation: Zoom, navigator, crosshairs, sync, context menu and animations are all Enterprise.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/umd/ag-charts-community.min.js was verified on file://.
libraries.reason: The free tier lacks nearly every IB chart type and all zoom and animation features. The useful parts require a commercial Enterprise licence.

libraries.name: IBM Carbon Charts
libraries.capabilities: Vanilla D3 SVG charts: alluvial (sankey), boxplot, bubble, bullet, choropleth (experimental), circle pack, combo, donut, gauge, heatmap, histogram, lollipop, meter, radar, treemap, tree and wordcloud.
libraries.interactions_animation: Zoom bar for time series, legend filtering and modest transitions.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/umd/bundle.umd.js plus styles.min.css. Verified (crashes with an en-US@posix locale).
libraries.reason: Permissive and accessible, but the look is locked to the IBM Carbon design language and hard to restyle into a pitchbook. Reference for accessibility and bullet-chart patterns.

libraries.name: ApexCharts
libraries.license: Proprietary dual licence since 5.1.0 (free only for orgs under US$2M revenue); last MIT release 5.0.0
libraries.capabilities: Line, area, bar, rangeBar, candlestick, boxplot, heatmap, treemap, radialBar, radar, polar, funnel. Premium-only features include waffle, raincloud and trellis.
libraries.interactions_animation: Smooth animations, zoom/pan toolbar and brush charts.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/apexcharts.min.js was verified on file://.
libraries.reason: The licence changed from MIT to proprietary in a minor version (5.0.0 to 5.1.0). A bank exceeds the US$2M cap, so it would need a paid Commercial or OEM licence. That is not acceptable for an open kit.

libraries.name: Highcharts
libraries.capabilities:
The most complete commercial suite.
- Core chart types plus Stock (navigator, technical indicators), Maps, Gantt, Dashboards and Grid.
- Variwide (Mekko), waterfall, dependency wheel, sankey, broken axis.
- Excellent accessibility module.
libraries.interactions_animation: Zoom, navigator, drilldown, exporting and good animations.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. highcharts.js plus modules, verified. Shows a credits link by default.
libraries.reason: Commercial. Client-facing reports need a SaaS licence. Use as a design and UX benchmark only (accessibility, broken axis, variwide, navigator).

libraries.name: amCharts 5
libraries.license: Freeware linkware: the amCharts logo/link must stay visible; a commercial licence removes it
libraries.capabilities: Full suite: XY, stock, maps (best-in-class), flow (sankey and chord), hierarchy (treemap, sunburst, force), gantt, venn, word cloud, radar and gauges.
libraries.interactions_animation: Best-in-class animation; cursor zoom, scrollbars and exporting plugin.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Heat rules and adapters for size and colour.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. index.js plus per-module scripts (not smoke-tested here; the jsdelivr listing timed out).
libraries.reason: A mandatory branding logo on every chart, or a paid licence, is unacceptable for client deliverables. Use as a motion and maps reference.

libraries.name: ZingChart
libraries.license: Proprietary 'Branded' free licence with a mandatory watermark; paid licences remove it
libraries.capabilities: Broad chart set including maps.
libraries.interactions_animation: Zoom, preview and animations.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. zingchart.min.js was verified (1.37 s render; the watermark shows off-localhost).
libraries.reason: The watermark is required unless paid, and the package has no OSI licence. Nothing to gain over ECharts.

libraries.name: TradingView Lightweight Charts
libraries.license: Apache-2.0 plus a mandatory TradingView attribution notice and link (NOTICE)
libraries.capabilities: High-performance financial price charts: candlestick, bar, line, area, baseline and histogram; multiple panes.
libraries.interactions_animation: Smooth pan, zoom and crosshair; no chart animation.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/lightweight-charts.standalone.production.js was verified (needs a valid Intl locale).
libraries.reason: The non-standard attribution requirement must be flagged for client PDFs. ECharts candlestick with dataZoom covers pitchbook price/volume charts.

libraries.name: KLineChart
libraries.capabilities: Candlestick/K-line with built-in technical indicators and drawing overlays.
libraries.interactions_animation: Pan, zoom and crosshair.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/umd/klinecharts.min.js was verified.
libraries.reason: A clean-licence alternative to Lightweight Charts if a trading-terminal widget is ever needed. Not needed for pitchbooks.

libraries.name: Recharts
libraries.capabilities: React SVG charts: line, bar, area, pie, radar, scatter, treemap, sankey and funnel.
libraries.interactions_animation: Brush, tooltips and animations.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Only umd/Recharts.js, which needs React and ReactDOM globals; React 19 no longer ships UMD.
libraries.reason: React-only. Unsuitable for a vanilla classic-script, file:// report kit.

libraries.name: Nivo
libraries.capabilities: React charts on D3: bar, line, pie, sankey, chord, treemap, sunburst, heatmap, calendar, choropleth, network, bump, marimekko and waffle.
libraries.interactions_animation: react-spring motion.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No UMD.
libraries.reason: React-only with no classic-script build. Nice chart vocabulary (marimekko, bump, calendar), useful as a design reference.

libraries.name: visx
libraries.capabilities: Low-level React visualisation primitives (D3 in React).
libraries.interactions_animation: DIY.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No UMD.
libraries.reason: React-only, low-level primitives. Not a fit for the vanilla kit.

libraries.name: Frappe Charts
libraries.capabilities: Simple SVG charts: bar, line, pie, percentage and heatmap.
libraries.interactions_animation: Basic.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/frappe-charts.min.umd.js.
libraries.reason: Last stable release was 2021, v2 has been stuck in release-candidate, and the chart vocabulary is narrow.

libraries.name: Taucharts
libraries.capabilities: Grammar-based D3 charts.
libraries.interactions_animation: Plugins for legend and tooltip.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Fails. dist/taucharts.min.js throws 'yn.format is not a function' because it expects an external d3 global.
libraries.reason: Abandoned since 2020 and broken standalone in our file:// test.

libraries.name: Chartist
libraries.capabilities: Minimal SVG line, bar and pie.
libraries.interactions_animation: CSS/SMIL animations; no interaction.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/index.umd.js plus index.css.
libraries.reason: Too minimal for IB needs.

libraries.name: Dygraphs
libraries.capabilities: Canvas time-series line charts with error bars.
libraries.interactions_animation: Zoom and range selector.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. dist/dygraph.min.js.
libraries.reason: Dated look and time series only. uPlot is a better dense-series complement.

libraries.name: Vizzu
libraries.capabilities: Animated transitions between chart types (morphing storytelling).
libraries.interactions_animation: Outstanding animated chart-to-chart morphs.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Channels: x, y, color, size, lightness, label.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No. ESM plus a cvizzu.wasm fetch; it failed on file:// with a CORS error.
libraries.reason: Fails the file:// gate. Keep as motion-design inspiration; ECharts universalTransition covers similar morphs.

libraries.name: Unovis
libraries.capabilities: Modular TS charts: XY, network graph, sankey, maps and timeline.
libraries.interactions_animation: Good.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No. ESM-only, with no UMD/IIFE dist; it would need esbuild pre-bundling.
libraries.reason: No classic-script build, and nothing it offers beyond ECharts for this use case.

libraries.name: BokehJS
libraries.capabilities: Python-first interactive plots: linked brushing via a shared ColumnDataSource, widgets and tables.
libraries.interactions_animation: Box zoom, pan, lasso, linked selection and CustomJS callbacks; no animation.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes. build/js/bokeh.min.js (plus widgets and tables). Bokeh output_file can be written with mode='relative'.
libraries.reason: A good analyst-side tool with a scientific look and a heavy bundle. Not suitable for pitchbook-grade client deliverables.

key_insights:
Keep ECharts 6.1.0 as the primary engine; the vendored full UMD (359 KB gz) is confirmed. Every v6 headline feature works from file:// in Chromium 141:
- chord
- beeswarm (xAxis.jitter + jitterOverlap:false)
- axis breaks (yAxis.breaks, plus expand/collapse/toggleAxisBreak actions)
- matrix coordinate system
- runtime chart.setTheme()
- registerCustomSeries

Default to the SVG renderer.
- In a Chromium PDF, SVG charts stayed vector with selectable text (pdftotext extracted the labels).
- A canvas chart was embedded as a 600x340 raster at ~104 ppi.
- Use canvas only above ~5k marks, with devicePixelRatio of at least 2 and a print snapshot on beforeprint.

think-cell-style exhibits are ECharts custom-series recipes of 20–40 lines each, all verified rendering cleanly:
- waterfall with dashed connectors and (negative) labels
- Marimekko on value x value axes
- football field (transparent stack + markLine)
- CAGR bracket via graphic + convertToPixel (recompute on resize)

The v6 axis break gives think-cell's broken value axis through bridge totals. Register these as named custom series (RK.series.*).
Custom series are not clipped by default; set clip:true. Combining yAxis.min with tall total bars otherwise overflows the grid; an axis break is the correct pitchbook fix.

Keep chart chrome in HTML: title, units, source and footnotes. In the test, an in-canvas title, legend and yAxis.name overlapped. HTML chrome also gives consistent typography, Ctrl+F, accessibility and cleaner PPT export.

ECharts 6 default-behaviour changes to guard against with a pinned theme and screenshot diffs:
- 6.0: new default theme with the legend at the bottom; anti-overflow axis layout (grid.outerBoundsMode); rich labels inherit plain label styles (richInheritPlainLabel); geo/graph center percent base changed.
- 6.1: containShape keeps edge bars inside the grid; tooltip.valueFormatter's 2nd argument is now rawDataIndex; axis.startValue is decoupled from min; an XSS in the lines tooltip was fixed.

ECharts Node SSR works from the same UMD file: init(null, null, {renderer:'svg', ssr:true}) then renderToSVGString(), about 60 ms per chart in Node 22. The Python builder can pre-render static SVG fallbacks for print, PPT, e-mail and thumbnails. echarts/ssr/client can hydrate them.

Locale gotcha: under LANG=C, headless Chromium reports navigator.language='en-US@posix', and uPlot, Carbon and Lightweight Charts then crash with 'Invalid language tag'. The Playwright PDF/PNG step must set locale:'en-US', and kit formatters must strip '@…' before calling Intl.NumberFormat.

Licence drift is real: ApexCharts moved from MIT (5.0.0, 2025-07-09) to a proprietary dual licence in 5.1.0, free only under US$2M revenue. Pin exact versions in vendor.json and re-run `npm view pkg@ver license` in CI before any bump.

AG Charts Community is a demo tier for IB use. Waterfall, sankey, heatmap, box-plot, candlestick, radar, funnel, treemap, zoom, navigator and animation all emit 'enterprise features' warnings and do not render.

Attribution and branding traps:
- Lightweight Charts (Apache-2.0 plus a mandatory TradingView notice and link)
- amCharts 5 (logo must stay unless paid)
- ZingChart (watermark)
- Highcharts (credits link; client-facing use needs a SaaS licence)

'ESM-only' does not mean no UMD: Vega 6 declares ESM-only, yet build/vega.min.js, vega-lite.min.js and vega-embed.min.js still ship and work on file://. Always check the jsdelivr dist listing. True ESM+WASM libraries (Vizzu, Perspective, DuckDB-WASM) fail on file:// because of CORS.

Vega-Lite is the right lazy-loaded complement for a future 'ask your data' console: declarative cross-filter params, bind:'scales' zoom, an expression-language calculate transform, JSON-schema validation of LLM output, and Altair interop. It has no animation and no sankey, chord or radar, so keep it out of printed pitchbook pages.

Python should emit kit component config plus a dataset, not raw ECharts options, because formatter functions cannot be JSON. JS components compile config into an option. Excel-like format codes (#,##0.0;(#,##0.0), 0.0x, 0.0%) should compile to JS formatters, since ECharts has no format-string system. pyecharts 2.1.0 already targets ECharts 6 assets.

For multi-dimensional encoding, ECharts visualMap is the workhorse: colour, colorAlpha, lightness, symbolSize, symbol and opacity per dimension, with several maps (6.1 seriesTargets). inRange/outOfRange styling doubles as instant cross-filter feedback. The tested bubble chart encoded x, y, size, colour (sector) and alpha (ROIC).

Cross-filter pattern: own the state store outside the engine.
1. ECharts brushSelected, legendselectchanged, datazoom or click events feed the store.
2. Each component calls setOption({dataset}, {replaceMerge:['dataset']}).
3. ECharts diff-animates the change.

Use universalTransition plus dataGroupId for drill and morph effects, echarts.connect for synced tooltips and zoom, and dispose() on re-mount.

Plotly 4 gotchas:
- Geo traces fetch topojson from cdn.plot.ly; preload via window.PlotlyGeoAssets.
- The new culori colour parser renders rgb() fractions near-black.
- mapbox traces were removed.
- The full bundle is 1.44 MB gz.
Category axes sort alphabetically by default in Vega-Lite and Observable Plot (the smoke test showed COGS, D&A, EBIT, Opex, Rev). Always pass an explicit order.
React-based libraries (Recharts, Nivo, visx, Victory, MUI X) are out: React 19 removed its UMD builds, and most of these have no classic-script dist.
